intro: I’m Anand Grandhi. I work at the intersection of product strategy, business operations and applied AI.

I joined BYJU’S in 2015, before its flagship learning app launched, and helped build and scale its learning products during five years of rapid growth. At Amazon, I worked on product adoption, customer experience and operational transformation.
Today, I help companies identify where AI can make a difference and how to put it into practice.

projects.title: Turning declining engagement into sustained product usage.
projects.summary: I transformed a declining daily engagement feature into a personalised experience, increasing return visits, retention and adoption of other product features.

blocks.p: Amazon had built an extensive learning ecosystem, but getting students to return regularly and discover relevant product features remained a challenge.

I identified the underlying barriers and proposed Daily Digest, a personalised daily experience combining behavioural science, relevant recommendations and short, actionable activities. I led the definition of the product logic and user journeys, collaborating with cross-functional teams on execution and continuous improvement.

Daily active users had declined from approximately 50,000 to 35,000. The existing Question of the Day served as an entry point to the product but lacked personalisation and meaningful connections to other features. I saw an opportunity to transform it into a driver of customer engagement, retention and broader product adoption.

figure.caption: Daily Digest within the learning ecosystem

blocks.p: I analysed customer behaviour and research findings to understand why students were not engaging consistently despite having access to an extensive learning library.
Three primary barriers emerged:

item: Time constraints
Students were balancing school, coaching and examination preparation.
Decision friction
Students struggled to identify what to study or practise next.
Perceived value
Students wanted immediate, relevant assistance with their individual weaknesses and examination preparation.

blocks.p: These insights informed the core product requirements for Daily Digest.
I translated customer pain points into specific behavioural interventions:

projects.title: Scaling personalised counselling through AI.
projects.summary: I developed an AI product strategy to increase counselling capacity without compromising personalisation. The strategy focused on reducing repetitive work, leveraging institutional knowledge and enabling better student-specific decisions.

blocks.p: Athena’s college admissions counselling model relies on understanding each student individually and guiding their academic and extracurricular development over several years. Increasing counselling capacity without compromising this personalisation was the central business challenge.

I examined the activities surrounding each counselling session. Counsellors spent time reviewing previous discussions, documenting conversations, updating Airtable records, tracking student commitments and researching suitable academic and extracurricular opportunities.
Another opportunity was Athena’s accumulated knowledge: approximately ten years of counselling recordings, documents and student records that could inform future counselling decisions.
I defined three AI product capabilities to support counsellors.

item: Transcript Intelligence

Convert counselling recordings into structured session summaries, extracting student interests, decisions, commitments and deadlines. Counsellors review the extracted information before updating student records.
Intelligent Counsellor Workbook

Maintain an evolving student profile covering academic progress, interests, achievements and pending activities. Before each session, counsellors receive a summary of previous discussions, outstanding commitments and changes in student circumstances.
Personalised Student Planning Engine

Recommend courses, competitions, internships and research opportunities based on student interests, academic goals, existing skills and availability. Check eligibility, prerequisites and deadlines before generating individual activity plans.

blocks.p: I defined a solution architecture combining structured student records, retrieval-augmented generation and business rules for eligibility and activity scheduling.

The reliability requirements addressed specific failures: invented student information, contradictory records, unsuitable opportunities and unrealistic time commitments. Consequential recommendations and record changes required counsellor approval.

framework.title: Counselling intelligence architecture
steps: Extract decisions, commitments and follow-ups from counselling conversations.
Maintain evolving student context, goals and milestones.
Combine student context and institutional knowledge to recommend feasible actions.
framework.caption: AI solution architecture.

blocks.p: I developed the product requirements, solution architecture and implementation roadmap, recommending that Athena begin with session documentation before introducing automated student profile updates and personalised planning.

overview: Athena needed to increase counselling capacity without losing the individual attention that its multi-year student guidance model depends on.
I defined the AI product strategy, prioritised three use cases and specified their requirements, architecture and reliability safeguards.
Delivered product requirements and an implementation roadmap for transcript intelligence, a counsellor workbook and personalised student planning.

blocks.p: WhiteTable was developing its product while establishing its internal operating processes. I examined how teams documented decisions, communicated requirements, planned work, collected customer feedback and approached customer acquisition.
I defined shared organisational knowledge and reusable AI workflows as the foundation for improving these processes.

Documentation was fragmented, meetings and decisions were not consistently recorded, and customer feedback lacked a structured collection process. Internal communication, work planning, task ownership and follow-ups required better coordination.

Software development lacked standardised PRDs, requirement specifications and consistent development workflows. Customer acquisition involved repetitive prospect discovery, research and outreach preparation.

projects.title: Building innovative learning products at scale.
projects.summary: I played a key role in building and scaling BYJU’S learning products during its rapid growth, leading multidisciplinary teams across product development, knowledge architecture, interactive learning and large-scale operations.

blocks.p: I joined BYJU’S before the launch of its flagship learning app and contributed to its product expansion over the following five years. As the business expanded across grades, subjects and product formats, my responsibilities grew from specialised team leadership to multidisciplinary product development and operations.
The expanding product portfolio required new capabilities, shared product frameworks and development processes that could support multiple initiatives simultaneously.
As the product ecosystem grew, connecting learning resources, assessments and individual user journeys became increasingly complex.

I led the development of a knowledge architecture across Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology, defining concept relationships, prerequisites and resource mapping. This provided a common foundation for product personalisation, recommendations, assessments and guided learning journeys.

blocks.p: My responsibilities covered defining product requirements, developing experience frameworks and coordinating execution across specialised teams.
Rapid product expansion required teams with expertise in subject knowledge, product development, design, media and technology.

I established multidisciplinary development workflows, product specifications, resource allocation processes and quality standards. These enabled teams to execute multiple product initiatives in parallel while maintaining consistency across the expanding product portfolio.
Over five years, I played a key role in establishing product capabilities, knowledge systems, teams and development processes that supported BYJU’S rapid growth.
My contribution extended across product innovation, capability building and operational execution at scale.

projects.title: Simplifying business operations through AI and automation.
projects.summary: I identified inefficiencies in everyday business operations and developed AI-enabled workflows to improve employee access to information, task tracking and internal communication.

blocks.p: As EMotorad expanded its operations, employees needed access to internal processes, training materials and standard operating procedures. Managers also needed visibility into pending work, task ownership and completion deadlines.
Through ARCHMATION, I identified the coordination bottlenecks and designed automated workflows around existing business tools.

Employees depended on colleagues and managers for routine questions about internal processes and SOPs. Training materials and process documentation required employees to search through multiple resources. Tracking pending activities, communicating deadlines and following up on incomplete tasks involved repetitive manual coordination.

item: Employee knowledge and training

I developed a workflow to organise internal documentation, SOPs and training materials into an accessible knowledge base. Employees could retrieve relevant information through natural-language queries, reducing dependence on individual team members.

figure.caption: HR onboarding automation with Google Drive

item: Task tracking and operational visibility

I developed workflows to consolidate pending activities, assigned responsibilities, completion dates and task status. Managers could review outstanding work without manually collecting updates from multiple employees.
Automated reminders and follow-ups
I designed automated notifications through WhatsApp and Gmail for upcoming deadlines, incomplete activities and pending responses. Reminders were linked to task status and completion dates.

projects.title: Transforming creative production with generative AI.
projects.summary: I developed generative AI solutions for clients across industries, building reusable production workflows for product photography, video, branding and architectural visualisation.

blocks.p: Through ARCHMATION, I worked with businesses across industries on creative production requirements, including product photography, commercial videos, branding and architectural visualisation.

Conventional production involved photography, location arrangements, physical samples, 3D modelling and multiple rounds of revisions. These requirements affected production costs, turnaround times and the number of creative variations clients could explore.
I evaluated creative production activities against cost, effort and client quality requirements to identify suitable applications of generative AI.

Early experimentation revealed several limitations: inconsistent product appearance, inaccurate proportions, limited control over composition and difficulty maintaining visual consistency across multiple outputs.
I developed repeatable workflows to address these limitations and adapt production methods to different client requirements.

item: Product photography and virtual try-on
Developed workflows for generating product photographs, lifestyle imagery and virtual try-on experiences, controlling product appearance, backgrounds, lighting and composition.
AI video production
Introduced generative video and AI presenter workflows for commercial videos, product demonstrations and branded communication, reducing dependence on conventional filming.
Architecture and design visualisation
Developed workflows for converting floor plans, reference images and design concepts into architectural visualisations, enabling faster exploration of design alternatives.

images.title: Product isolation to staged scene and video

item: Branding and creative production
Developed reusable workflows for campaign imagery, moodboards, branded assets and creative variations while maintaining visual consistency.

blocks.p: I established workflows covering client requirements, reference inputs, model selection, generation, quality checks and approval.
Depending on the application, I used ComfyUI, FLUX, SDXL, ControlNet and customised model training to improve control over generated outputs.

images.title: Character views and parallel 3D model outputs

blocks.p: Standardising these workflows allowed the team to reuse production methods across client engagements and reduce repeated experimentation.

As co-founder, I managed client requirements, evaluated commercial opportunities, defined solution approaches and coordinated production. My work combined business development, technology experimentation, workflow development and production management.
